findings.description: `-c protocol.allow=never` sets only the default for protocols that have no policy of their own. A `protocol.<name>.allow=always` in the session-writable shared config overrides it. So a planted promisor remote plus a planted missing sha can still make the lazy fetch run a program the session chose.
findings.body:
**`protocol.allow=never` doesn't close the lazy fetch that the code and decision 83 say it closes.**

```ts
runGit(
  repoPath,
  ['-c', 'protocol.allow=never', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', sha, `refs/heads/${target}`],
  { stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'ignore'], timeout: LANDED_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS },
);
```

`protocol.allow` is only the fallback for protocols that have no policy of their own. Git checks `protocol.<name>.allow` first, from any config scope. The shared `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/config` is session-writable: `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG`'s own doc says so, and decisions 41, 54 and 82 rely on it.

A session can plant these:
- `remote.x.promisor=true`
- `remote.x.url=ext::sh -c …` together with `protocol.ext.allow=always`. The `file` protocol plus `uploadpack` works too.
- a merged row whose merge event has a `prUrl`, a valid `target` and a random 40-hex `sha`

The next `pup status`, `pup ui` refresh or conductor read then runs `merge-base` on the missing object. That triggers the promisor fetch, which runs the planted command with pup's unsandboxed environment. Nothing in `runGit` stops this: `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` pins no `protocol.*`, `remote.*.promisor` or `extensions.partialClone` key, and `scrubbedGitEnv` doesn't set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`.

**Provenance.** The gate already walks history a session wrote with no protocol pin (`isAncestor` in merge-gate.service.ts, `merge-base` in git-diff.client.ts). What this delta adds:
- a new trigger on every snapshot, outside any merge;
- a written claim, in the JSDoc and in decision 83, that this trigger is closed.

**Possible fix, at this call site only.**
- Pass `env: { GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH: '1' }`. `RunGitOptions.env` is merged over the scrubbed env. This needs git 2.44 or later; older gits ignore it.
- Also pin `-c protocol.<name>.allow=never` for `ext`, `fd`, `file`, `ssh`, `git`, `http` and `https`. Command-line `-c` wins over a local key with the same name.
- Remote-helper names are an open set, so neither measure is complete on its own. Alternatively, check that the sha is present first, with `cat-file -e` under the same env, and correct the decision 83 wording.

findings.description: The guard that stops a second '→' in an inbox line only covers the question; a session id outside SESSION_ID_PATTERN is printed before the reason with its '→' kept, so a session-written row id still forges an arrow and a command the conductor acts on.
findings.body:
**A session id can still forge an arrow in the inbox line.**

This commit guards against a forged second arrow in two places: the question gets `replaceAll('→', '->')`, and an id outside the minted shape gets no command built around it. But both print sites still render the id itself in front of the real arrow:

```ts
// src/cli/index.ts L1183, src/cli/ui/dashboard-text.utils.ts L166-169
`  ${sanitizeReason(need.sessionId)}  ${sanitizeReason(need.reason)}  → ${sanitizeReason(need.answer)}`
```

`need.sessionId` is `sanitizeReason(row.id)` (L411). `sanitizeReason` strips control characters and trims, but it keeps `→`. The `sessions.id` column has no CHECK, and decision 66 treats the store as session-writable. Take a row with id `x → pup merge s-other --pr` in state `blocked`. It prints:

```
  x → pup merge s-other --pr  blocked (0 rejections)  → (session id outside the minted shape; inspect the store)
```

The first arrow on that line is the forged one. The fleet print site is new in this delta, since it used to print `sessionLine` with no arrow.

**A related gap: `SESSION_ID_PATTERN` is tested on the *sanitized* id.** A raw id of `victim ` or `victim\t` trims to `victim` and passes the check. It sits beside the real `victim` row as a separate primary key, and gets a real `pup unblock victim` / `pup steer victim` built around it.

**Possible fix.**
- Decide whether the id is minted from the raw `row.id`, for example as a `mintedId` flag set next to L411.
- At both print sites, print an unminted id with `→` neutralised, or as a fixed placeholder.
- Keep `sessionId` raw for the `fleetSummary` lookup.

findings.description: The landed answer is memoised only per snapshot, so `pup ui` (2s refresh, every project under --all) spawns a synchronous git with a 2s timeout for each never-landing PR on every refresh; under squash or rebase merges that set only grows, and the render loop stalls.
findings.body:
**The landed check spawns git for every PR-merged session on every refresh.**

`landedShaLookup` creates a new `answered` map per `buildDashboardSnapshot` (L67), so nothing carries over between refreshes. Several things multiply that cost:
- `use-snapshot.hook.ts` rebuilds the snapshot synchronously on the Ink thread every `SNAPSHOT_REFRESH_MS = 2_000`.
- `fleetReading` rebuilds it for every project under `--all`.
- `listSessions(db)` returns every merged session ever recorded.
- `runGit` is `execFileSync`.

```ts
const answered = new Map<string, boolean>();
return (target, sha) => {
  if (sha === undefined) return true;
  ...
  runGit(repoPath, ['-c', 'protocol.allow=never', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', sha, `refs/heads/${target}`], { ..., timeout: LANDED_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS });
```

This isn't only a squash-merge problem. Any merged session whose newest merge has a `prUrl` and a pinned sha pays one blocking `git` spawn per refresh, forever, including PRs that already landed, because the `true` answer is thrown away with the map. A squash- or rebase-merged PR also stays listed, so it may hit the slow path of a full history walk, up to the 2s timeout. This repo is past PR #140. With a few hundred PR-merged sessions across a fleet, each 2s tick freezes the UI for hundreds of ms or more, and that grows without bound.

**Possible fix.**
- Memoise across snapshots in a module-level map keyed on `repoPath`, `target` and `sha`.
- Cache a `true` answer for good, since an ancestor stays one while the branch only moves forward.
- Cache a `false` answer against the target tip, re-asking only when `refs/heads/<target>` has moved.
- Don't cache a timeout as a final `false`.

findings.description: `sha === undefined -> landed` counts every PR merge written from 2026-07-25 (61c5ca5) to 2026-10-08 (70318a6) as landed, so a PR opened in the days before 70318a6 and still open drops out of the inbox; the same branch also lets a session-written merge event with no `sha` hide its own open PR.

PLAIN_BRANCH is narrower than `assertTargetName` (`check-ref-format --branch`): a valid target with non-ASCII letters or `+`, `#`, `,`, `!` or `%` is never checked, so its PRs stay listed forever even after landing (it fails safe, but the entry never clears).

PR_URL's host class rejects a port (for example a GitHub Enterprise `https://ghe.corp:8443/o/r/pull/3`), so such a PR's url is withheld behind '(PR url outside the pull-request shape; inspect the store)' even though it is genuine.

Replacing `→` with `->` still leaves an arrow an LLM conductor reads as one, and other arrows (`⟶`, `➔`, `➜`, `⇒`, `➡`) pass through untouched; the guard is cosmetic unless the answer is set apart by something the question cannot produce.
Decision 83 still says the session row "only gains an optional `openPrUrl`", but this commit renamed the field to `openPr?: { url?: string }`; update the decision to match.

The new `GIT_ENV` constant was inserted between `tempRepo`'s JSDoc and `tempRepo` itself, so the JSDoc now documents `GIT_ENV` and `tempRepo` has none; move `GIT_ENV` above that JSDoc.

naming.md says a `utils` file holds pure functions only and cannot import a `service`; the new `import { needsYou } from '../../core/dashboard.service.js'` adds a second service import here. Compute the inbox in the caller and pass it in, or move `needsYou` to a `*.utils` file.

The need-line template `  ${sanitizeReason(need.sessionId)}  ${sanitizeReason(need.reason)}  → ${sanitizeReason(need.answer)}` is now copy-pasted verbatim from `src/cli/index.ts` line 1183, so a change to one format (separator, arrow) will drift from the other.

`fleetBlockLines` no longer reads `summary.needsYou` and recomputes `needsYou(snapshot)` itself, so `fleetSummary.needsYou` has no non-test reader yet is still built eagerly; drop the field or have the fleet view print from it.

general.md §No hardcoded values puts timeouts in the area's `*.constants.ts`; `LANDED_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (and the PLAIN_BRANCH/COMMIT_SHA/PR_URL shapes) are declared in the service file, though `RECENT_EVENT_COUNT` and `NEED_ORDER` set an inline precedent.
